records.text: Charlie Kirk said Lyndon Baines Johnson, parts of the U.S. government, and Cubans wanted JFK dead.
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: But definitely, Lyndon Baines Johnson and parts of our own government and the Cubans wanted him dead.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Kirk made the accusation. Current authoritative records do not substantiate that Lyndon Johnson, parts of the U.S. government, and Cubans wanted Kennedy dead. The House committee found no institutional involvement by the Secret Service, FBI, or CIA and found that the Cuban government was not involved, while leaving open only the possibility that unidentified individual anti-Castro Cubans may have participated. Those findings do not establish personal intent by Johnson or the broad groups named, so the allegation cannot be resolved conclusively.

sources.title: House Select Committee on Assassinations Findings on Conspiracy
sources.relevance: Official findings reject institutional U.S. and Cuban-government involvement while leaving limited individual possibilities open.

records.text: There were 15 or 20 inexcusable things that happened on the day of JFK's assassination: they changed the parade route, he rode in an open air convertible, LBJ decided not to ride alongside him, and the vehicle slowed down right when it went by the Texas schoolbook depository
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: There were like 15 or 20 things that happened that day that were inexcusable. They changed the parade route. He rode in an open air convertible. LBJ (Lyndon Baines Johnson) decided not to ride alongside of him. The vehicle slowed down right when it went by the Texas schoolbook depository.

verification.notes: Several components are documented: Kennedy rode in an open limousine, the vice president rode in a separate car, and the motorcade slowed for the Houston-to-Elm turn. But the Warren Commission says the motorcade followed the planned route, that the route had been publicized before the assassination, and that the limousine maintained an average 11.2 mph over the 186 feet immediately preceding the fatal head shot. Calling the route a last-minute change and saying the vehicle slowed specifically at the Depository are not supported by these records. The numeric claim of 15 or 20 inexcusable events is evaluative and not independently verifiable.

sources.title: Warren Commission Report, Chapter 2: The Assassination
sources.relevance: Documents the planned route, open limousine, motorcade configuration, turn speed, and limousine speed before the shots.

sources.title: Dallas Times Herald clipping with map of motorcade route

records.text: Owens said Lyndon Baines Johnson was clearly implicated in JFK's assassination.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Lyndon Baines Johnson, who was clearly implicated in JFK's assassination.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens made the accusation. Current authoritative records reviewed do not establish that Lyndon Johnson was implicated in Kennedy's assassination. The Warren Commission found no conspiracy, while the later House committee found a probable unidentified conspiracy but no official U.S. agency involvement and did not implicate Johnson. Lack of substantiation is not direct proof that the accusation is false, so the result is unverifiable.

appearances.snippet: And I do kind of feel like the military cult has been in power since LBJ helped murder JFK, set him up and then I think cleaned house and put in his guys in the military. That's how I feel anyways.

verification.notes: The official investigative record found Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone and found no credible evidence of a broader conspiracy involving Lyndon Johnson. Later document releases have not produced substantiated evidence that LBJ arranged Kennedys murder or a cover-up.
